# Bundled Bouncy Castle: how it is made and how to update it

Jacksum bundles a **stripped** and **relocated** copy of [Bouncy Castle](https://www.bouncycastle.org)
(BC) in `src/main/java/net/jacksum/zzadopt/org/bouncycastle`, package `net.jacksum.zzadopt.org.bouncycastle`. It contains only the classes that Jacksum's
own code needs, directly or transitively (about 80 of the more than 3000 BC source files).

**Do not edit `src/main/java/net/jacksum/zzadopt/org/bouncycastle` by hand.** The tree is generated by `bouncycastle/update-bc.sh` from

1. the pristine BC sources (`bcprov-jdk18on-<version>-sources.jar` from Maven Central),
2. `overlay/`: whole files that replace or add to upstream files,
3. `patches/`: unified diffs against the pristine upstream files.

### Relocation

Up to Jacksum 4.0.1 the copy lived in its original package `org.bouncycastle`. If Jacksum is used as a
library together with a real Bouncy Castle, both jars then provide the same classes, and whichever comes
first on the classpath wins: the application could get Jacksum's stripped classes (e.g. the no-op
`CryptoServicesRegistrar` or the pinned BC 1.73 digests below), or Jacksum could get a different BC version
than the one it has been verified with. In JPMS it is a split package. Therefore `update-bc.sh` relocates
the tree to `net.jacksum.zzadopt.org.bouncycastle`, like the other adopted code in `net.jacksum.zzadopt`.

The relocation is a mechanical last step: every `org.bouncycastle` in package, import, Javadoc and
fully qualified references becomes `net.jacksum.zzadopt.org.bouncycastle` (not in URLs such as
`www.bouncycastle.org`). The script stops if a needed file contains a string literal with the package
name (a property or class name, whose meaning the relocation would change). `overlay/`, `patches/` and
`files.txt` stay in the **upstream namespace** (`org/bouncycastle/...`), so patches apply to the pristine
sources and overlay files can be diffed against upstream directly.

Every Jacksum modification of BC code lives in `overlay/` or `patches/` and nowhere else. Each one
starts with a `JACKSUM-MOD:` comment that gives the reason, the upstream state and the condition under
which it can be removed. `files.txt` lists every generated file and where it comes from
(`upstream`, `patched` or `overlay`).

The current version, the SHA-256 of the sources jar and the commit of the test data are recorded in
`bc.properties`.

## Updating to a new BC version

```
bouncycastle/update-bc.sh 1.87                    # or without argument: regenerate bc.version
mvn clean package                                  # clean is required, see below
bouncycastle/verify/compare-jars.sh <old-jacksum.jar> target/jacksum-<version>.jar
git diff --stat -- src/main/java/net/jacksum/zzadopt/org/bouncycastle bouncycastle/files.txt
```

Build the old jar **before** you run the update (or keep a released jar around), because
`compare-jars.sh` needs it.

Always build with `mvn clean package` after an update. An incremental build over the replaced tree can
produce a jar in which no algorithm works at all (`NullPointerException` in
`HashFunctionFactory.getHashFunction()`, seen in October 2026).

What `update-bc.sh` does:

1. downloads the sources jar (cached under `target/bc-update/<version>`) and checks it against the
   SHA-1 published on Maven Central and, for the version in `bc.properties`, against the recorded SHA-256;
2. extracts `org/bouncycastle/**` and applies `patches/*.patch`. If a patch does not apply, the script
   stops. Check whether the bug has been fixed upstream: if so, delete the patch, otherwise rebase it;
3. copies `overlay/` over the patched tree and relocates the result to `net.jacksum.zzadopt.org.bouncycastle`
   (see above);
4. compiles Jacksum's own sources (`src/main/java/net` without the generated tree) with
   `javac -implicit:class -sourcepath <relocated tree>`.
   javac reads exactly the BC source files that are needed transitively, so there is **no list of
   required classes to maintain**: a new BC algorithm used in `MDbouncycastle` brings its dependencies
   along automatically. The script also warns about overlay files that are no longer used. If javac fails
   because BC has removed a class that Jacksum still needs, the script names the class and prints the
   commands to pin it (see below);
5. stops if heavy BC infrastructure (`asn1`, `math/ec`, `jcajce`, `jce`, `pqc`) shows up, which usually
   means that a new upstream dependency must be covered by the overlay (see `CryptoServicesRegistrar` below).
   It also prints a `NOTE` for every needed upstream class that is deprecated, because such a class will
   probably be removed some day (currently `AsconDigest` and `AsconXof`, see below);
6. runs the official LWC hash known answer tests (`verify/LwcKat.java`, test vectors from
   [bc-test-data](https://github.com/bcgit/bc-test-data), downloaded at the commit in `bc.properties`)
   for Ascon, Esch (Sparkle), PHOTON-Beetle and Xoodyak. **The tree is replaced only if all vectors pass**;
7. replaces `src/main/java/net/jacksum/zzadopt/org/bouncycastle`, copies BC's `LICENSE.java` and writes `files.txt` (and removes the old, not relocated
   tree `src/main/java/org/bouncycastle` if it still exists);
8. updates `bc.properties`.

`compare-jars.sh` then computes every algorithm (`-a all`) over inputs of critical lengths (0 bytes,
block boundaries, more than 64 KiB, 1 MiB), a few HMACs, `--info` of the BC based XOFs/LWC hashes and the
`--hmacs` list with both jars and diffs the output. Any difference must be understood before you
release.

### When BC removes a class that Jacksum still needs

Example: BC has deprecated `AsconDigest` and `AsconXof` (Ascon v1.2), Jacksum uses them on purpose (see
below). If a future BC version removes them, `update-bc.sh` stops in step 4 and prints something like

```
These classes have been removed in BC 1.xx, but Jacksum still needs them:
    org/bouncycastle/crypto/digests/AsconXof.java
Either adapt Jacksum's code, or pin each class from the current tree into the overlay
(the overlay is in the upstream namespace, so the copy is relocated back to org.bouncycastle):
    mkdir -p bouncycastle/overlay/org/bouncycastle/crypto/digests && sed 's/net\.jacksum\.zzadopt\.org\.bouncycastle/org.bouncycastle/g' src/main/java/net/jacksum/zzadopt/org/bouncycastle/crypto/digests/AsconXof.java > bouncycastle/overlay/org/bouncycastle/crypto/digests/AsconXof.java
```

The current tree still holds the old version at that point, because it is replaced only in step 7. The
`sed` turns the copy back into the pristine upstream file. To pin a class:

1. run the printed commands;
2. add a `JACKSUM-MOD:` header to the pinned file (from which BC version it is, why it is pinned);
3. run the update again. If javac then misses further classes (e.g. package-private base classes such as
   `AsconBaseDigest` or `AsconXofBase`, or classes whose API has changed incompatibly), pin them in the same
   way;
4. add the pinned files to the table of modifications below.

The known answer tests in step 6 cover Ascon-Hash, Ascon-HashA, Ascon-XOF and Ascon-XOFa, so a pinned Ascon
class is verified automatically.

After an update, also:

- document it in `RELEASE-NOTES.txt`,
- check the BC copyright year in `src/main/resources/net/jacksum/legal/copyright.txt` against
  `src/main/java/net/jacksum/zzadopt/org/bouncycastle/LICENSE.java`,
- try to drop overlay files and patches whose "remove when" condition has become true (delete them and
  run the update again, the known answer tests and `compare-jars.sh` tell you whether that works).

## Jacksum's modifications

State: BC 1.86, October 2026.

| Where | What | Why | Remove when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overlay/org/bouncycastle/crypto/CryptoServicesRegistrar.java` | no-op stub of `checkConstraints()` | since BC 1.72 most digests call `CryptoServicesRegistrar.checkConstraints()` in their constructors; the real registrar pulls in ~170 further classes (ASN.1, EC math, DH/DSA parameters, ...). Jacksum does not use BC's service constraints | never (by design). Extend it if a new BC version references another method (javac fails then) |
| `overlay/org/bouncycastle/crypto/digests/XoodyakDigest.java` | pinned to pristine BC 1.73 | BC 1.86 fails the official KAT, Count = 1 (empty message): `8dd8d589...` instead of `EA152F2B...` | a newer BC passes `xoodyak_LWC_HASH_KAT_256.txt` |
| `overlay/org/bouncycastle/crypto/digests/PhotonBeetleDigest.java` | pinned to pristine BC 1.73 | BC 1.86 fails the official KAT, Count = 17 (16-byte message `000102...0F`) | a newer BC passes `photonbeetle_LWC_HASH_KAT_256.txt` |
| `patches/0001-blake2bp-buffer-length.patch` | `8*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES` becomes `PARALLELISM_DEGREE*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES` in `Blake2bpDigest.update()` | the buffer is only 4 * 128 bytes long; messages > 512 bytes fed in pieces cause an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` or a wrong hash. Present in BC 1.73 to 1.86 | fixed upstream (the patch no longer applies) |

Modifications that are **outside** of the generated tree, in Jacksum's own code:

| Where | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `src/main/java/net/jacksum/algorithms/md/TigerDigest_192_4_PHP_version.java` | copy of BC 1.71's `TigerDigest` with extra rounds and a register swap in `processBlock()` (marked `<BEGIN>`/`<END>`) | PHP's `tiger192,4`, `tiger160,4`, `tiger128,4`. It is Jacksum's own variant, so it does not belong in the generated tree |
| `src/main/java/net/jacksum/algorithms/wrappers/MDbouncycastle.java` | `createAsconV12()` uses the deprecated `AsconDigest` and `AsconXof` on purpose, with `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")` | ascon-hash, ascon-hasha, ascon-xof and ascon-xofa are Ascon v1.2. Their BC successors `AsconHash256`, `AsconXof128` and `AsconCXof128` (NIST SP 800-232) are different algorithms (little-endian, different padding and IVs) with different hash values, and HashA/XofA have no successor. If BC removes the classes, pin them (see above) |
| `src/main/java/net/jacksum/algorithms/wrappers/MDbouncycastle.java` | KangarooTwelve and MarsupilamiFourteen are finalized with `Xof.doFinal(out, 0, 32 / 64)` | since BC 1.71 the `Kangaroo` constructors ignore the requested output length (the default is 16 / 32 bytes). Up to Jacksum 4.0.1 `Kangaroo.java` was pinned to BC 1.69 for that reason |

## History: modifications that are no longer needed

The tree that was in use up to Jacksum 4.0.1 was stripped by hand from BC 1.69 (Kangaroo), 1.71 (most
files) and 1.73 (Blake2b/2s/2bp/2sp/2xs, Blake3, Ascon, Sparkle, Xoodyak, PHOTON-Beetle). A diff
against the pristine upstream jars (October 2026) showed these local changes, which BC 1.86 together with
the overlay above makes unnecessary:

- `Blake2bDigest`, `Blake2sDigest`, `Blake3Digest`: the calls of `CryptoServicesRegistrar.checkConstraints()`
  and the import were commented out. Replaced by the stub.
- `Blake2spDigest`: buffer length fix (`8 * BLAKE2S_BLOCKBYTES`). Fixed upstream.
- `Kangaroo`: pinned to BC 1.69. Replaced by the XOF call in `MDbouncycastle`.
- `AsconDigest`: `implements ExtendedDigest` with `getByteLength() == 8` (the block size for `--info`
  and HMAC). BC 1.86 does the same.
- `PhotonBeetleDigest`: algorithm name "PHOTON-Beetle Hash". Not used by Jacksum.
- About 40 files: only added `@param`/`@return` Javadoc, `@Deprecated` and `@SuppressWarnings`. Not
  needed, because the Javadoc doclint checks only `net.jacksum.*` and `net.loefflmann.*` (see `pom.xml`).
- The GOST classes were unchanged apart from Javadoc.

## Verification of the switch to BC 1.86

- All 8 LWC hash KAT files (1025 vectors each) pass, both with a fresh instance and after `reset()` with
  byte-wise updates.
- `compare-jars.sh` with Jacksum 4.0.2 before and after the switch: all ~10,000 lines identical,
  except that `--info` now reports a block size of 16 bytes for esch256 and esch384 (`SparkleDigest` is
  an `ExtendedDigest` in BC 1.86). HMAC is not affected: Jacksum rejects HMAC for algorithms whose
  block size is smaller than the digest size.
